verifications.claim: The NASA Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket successfully propelled four astronauts into Earth orbit to begin a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA rocket blasted off... lifting four astronauts toward space... SLS rocket... 10-day mission'; R2: 'Four astronauts... Artemis II mission... 10 days'; R3: 'four astronauts... ten day mission'; R6: 'four astronauts... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state SLS launched four astronauts to Earth orbit for 10-day lunar mission.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is currently operating normally in orbit after passing initial checks.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion spacecraft separated... mission seemed to be mostly going well... checking out key systems'; R2: 'Orion... on a slingshot “free return” trajectory... performing really well'; R3: 'Orion is being put to the test - and passing... life-support systems... working normally'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Orion in orbit, performing well, and passing tests, but mention minor issues (e.g., comms, toilet); not precisely 'operating normally after initial checks' but broadly supports.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972... first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years'; R2: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R3: 'first time since 1972 during Apollo 17, human beings have left Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.
